spec.cue: Watch what the spider's principal eyes pick out. Sharp at the centre, blurred at the edge, and the scene turns when the spider looks.

rows: The principal eyes resolve fine detail. Portia fimbriata reaches about 12.5 cycles per degree, close to a person's sharpness, but only in a small central zone of the picture.
Each principal eye sees a narrow upright strip about 2 degrees wide and about 21 degrees high. Side eyes cover most of the rest of the circle.
Across all four pairs of eyes, a salticid sees about 360 degrees around it, although only the principal pair sees fine detail.
The principal retinas sweep side to side across a target, about 2 degrees at a time, with a period of about 1 to 1.3 seconds. A quick saccade of 15 degrees completes within a tenth of a second.
The blur falloff, the fading of still things, the colour channels, the hold time and the strength of pull toward movement are the app's drawing, not records. They are set by the app.

claims.how: Portia fimbriata principal eye resolution of 12.5 cycles per degree (R12) matches R4's 12.5 cycles per degree.
Four pairs of eyes give a 360 degree field of view, stated for salticids in general; graded g because the species is not measured.
The principal retina is about 2 degrees wide and about 21 high (R14); graded g in this draft because the strip width is from a Phidippus record and the field from a wider salticid group.
Salticids perceive flicker up to 40 Hz; the app keeps a person's rate, so the value is the family figure, graded g.
A 15 degree saccade is complete within 0.1 s in Metaphidippus harfordi.
Side-to-side sweeps of about 2 degrees with a period of 1.1 to 1.3 s, from Metaphidippus harfordi (R94) and Phidippus and Metaphidippus (R89).
The central sharp strip uses the principal eye resolution of 12.5 cycles per degree.

quotes.quote: The highest value of the spatial resolving power (Nyquist frequency) of the principle eyes of jumping spiders, such as Portia fimbriata Doleschell, 1859, is 12.5 cycles/degree
Combined, the four pairs of eyes give the spider a 360° field of view.

The anterior medial eyes (AMEs) are referred to as principal eyes and are movable, with a small visual field of around 5 deg each, but with high spatial resolution and color vision.
